scope: Primary source research for five EOR teaching cases. Raw small licensed numerical files; no fabricated field/lab truth.
important_findings: e1: no small design-parameter / production-response supervised corpus verified; use transparent analytical PKN teaching simulator with SI units, no oil-gain labels.
e2: a licensed processed field microseismic catalog is available; it has event locations, not fracture masks, fracture-tip ground truth or oil recovery.
e3: verified small real laboratory polymer dataset has 15 resistance-factor rows and 5 viscosity/recovery pairs. It cannot support high-dimensional recipe optimization.
e4: verified real field monthly source has 1127 rows and 20 Operation/UID groups (19 distinct Scheme names because Hangingstone is repeated). 3 CSS facilities give 180 rows; other 947 are SAGD.

e5: verified laboratory biosurfactant production CSV has 4 fermentation batches, each 16 offline assays (64 labels total), plus ~21600 sensor points/batch. Do not count interpolated assays as measured labels.

sources.role: primary physical benchmark basis; recommend independently implemented teaching simulation
sources.title: Viscosity-Storage-Dominated PKN Hydraulic Fracture — GEOS validation study
sources.license: New teaching simulation should use project license; formulas are reimplemented from cited benchmark, no simulator code needs to be copied.

units.Q: m3/s total injection rate; preserve same convention as benchmark

sources.recommended_experiment: Parameter sweep -> train a surrogate -> predict held-out combinations -> maximize modeled half length under explicit net-pressure and injected-volume constraints; compare optimizer result to analytical response. Restrict to viscosity-storage PKN assumptions, homogeneous rock, fixed height, negligible leakoff; filter to l/h well above 1.
sources.split: Group by complete (E, nu, height) rock scenario; do not split time samples from one scenario into both train and test.
sources.label_guardrail: Use modeled fracture geometry/pressure, never measured recovery, causal oil gain, field optimum or NPV.
sources.primary_basis: GEOS validation documentation cites Kovalyshen and Detournay (2010) and Economides and Nolte (2000) for the PKN analytical solutions.

sources.title: Hydraulic Fracture Propagation, Arrest, and Closure Simulations using PyFrac
sources.decision: Not a ready numerical dataset under 30 MB. Main outputs ZIP is 46168199 bytes. Small postprocessor is a Mathematica notebook; small Python script uses dimensionless inputs with many parameters set to 1. Do not relabel as dimensional measurements.

sources.title: Utah FORGE: Phase-Picking Based Microseismic Event Catalog - April 2024 Stimulation
sources.authors: Weiqiang Zhu; Junhao Song; Eyal Shimony; Ariel Lellouch; Uri Wygodny; Xiaoming Zhang; Noam Zach Dvory
sources.kind: processed observed field seismic event catalog, enhanced geothermal stimulation; domain transfer to oil EOR must be explicit

units.depth_km: km, catalog coordinate reference, not automatically depth below ground
units.adloc_residual_time: residual time; likely seconds but unit not explicitly verified in CSV header

sources.target_availability: No true fracture extent, masks, treatment parameters or oil gain. Event locations and uncertainties can support geometric fit/uncertainty exercises, not supervised fracture reconstruction accuracy.
sources.recommended_experiment: Transform lat/lon to a local meter coordinate system, retain uncertainty, use robust weighted plane/ellipsoid fit or rasterize density for CV preprocessing. Compare PCA baseline to robust optimization with held-out spatial residual and bootstrap stability. Call it microseismic event-cloud extent proxy; if true segmentation training is needed create explicitly synthetic fracture images/masks in an independent teaching simulator.
sources.split: Group by acquisition day or stimulation stage if joined to primary stage metadata; no random event split claimed independent. Do not infer true fracture boundaries from event-cloud hull.

sources.title: Data for: Performance of Enlarging Swept Volume by Surface-active Polymer Flooding for Enhancing Oil Recovery
sources.author: Qiannan Yu
sources.local_file: Data for Performance of Enlarging Swept Volume by Surface-active Polymer Flooding for Enhancing Oil Recovery.xlsx
sources.kind: laboratory results; workbook contains several unrelated plots/tables in one sheet. Only use the clearly headed tables.

units.permeability: 10^-3 micrometer^2 as explicitly headed BQ1, values 100/200/500; do not silently call these mD
units.recovery_increase: percentage points; source labels increments as %

sources.extraction: BP3:BS17 gives serial, permeability, concentration (forward fill only within merged BR cells), resistance factor. BW4:CA8 gives viscosity, linked-polymer and surface-active-polymer recoveries/increments. Explicit shared waterflood baseline BV4:BV8=23.67. Do not treat concentration-group averages BT as independent samples.
sources.recommended_experiment: Tiny Gaussian-process regression or monotone interpolation; minimize concentration to meet a user-selected resistance factor within observed permeability range. Report uncertainty and measured support. Recovery table is a separate five-point experiment and must not be joined to concentration rows to invent recovery labels.
sources.split: Leave one concentration group out (5 folds, 3 rows/fold); separately leave one permeability level out to reveal extrapolation. Only 15 measured labels; avoid deep models or impressive accuracy claims.
sources.label_guardrail: No surfactant concentration input in the selected table, no multicomponent recipe optimum, no field recovery or causal oil gain.

sources.title: Data Mining and Unsupervised Machine Learning in Canadian In Situ Oil Sands Database for Knowledge Discovery and Carbon Cost Analysis
sources.paper_dataset_version: 10.17632/8ngkgz69zb.4; public API v4 returns byte-identical file/hash as v2 checked here
sources.author: Minxing Si
sources.kind: observed scheme-level monthly field operation aggregates extracted from Petrinex
sources.group_key: Operation or UID, not Scheme (Hangingstone has two operations)

units.SteamINJ: m3 cold water equivalent per month at 15 C
units.SGF: 10^3 m3 fuel gas per month at 15 C and 101.325 kPa absolute
units.FuelINJ: gas injection, 10^3 m3/month; verify exact semantic field if used

sources.units_basis: Source article Table 2 and following paragraph explicitly specify oil/steam m3, gas 10^3 m3, steam cold-water equivalent and standard conditions.
sources.recommended_experiment: For CSS task subset Method=CSS, compare persistence/seasonal naive baseline to lagged ridge/random-forest next-month production forecast with previous oil, previous steam and seasonal terms. Evaluate MAE in m3/month and normalized error. If adding a steam-constrained what-if, label it an assumed heating/production simulation or observational scenario, not causal uplift optimization.
sources.split: Train 2015-2017, validation 2018, test 2019 within operations; also leave one CSS Operation out to demonstrate cross-facility generalization. Fit scaling/imputation on train only. Gaps should break sequences or be flagged.
leakage: Same-month SOR contains Oil target directly; never use SOR to predict same-month Oil.
Do not shift/roll across operation boundaries.
Scheme aggregates cannot identify individual injection/soak/production cycles.
sources.label_guardrail: No well-level controls, soak duration, steam quality or measured counterfactual, so no per-cycle optimum or causal oil increase.

sources.title: Production and separation of a trehalolipid biosurfactant: data
sources.authors: Peter Martin; Sara Bages Estopa; James Winterburn; Colin Webb; Dan White
sources.kind: measured ex-situ Rhodococcus sp. PML026 laboratory fermentation; MEOR-relevant biosurfactant production, not reservoir microbial activity or recovery
sources.time: 0 to 360 hours; offline assay interval 24 hours
sources.recommended_experiment: Forecast the next 24-h trehalolipid concentration or biomass. Compare persistence to ridge/low-complexity kinetic-informed regression; fit on training batches with only past assays and past sensor-window summaries. Show uncertainty and an explicit 64-label limitation. B2a and B2b are reported replicates; keep them together for genuine process generalization or use them explicitly for replicate reproducibility evaluation.
sources.split: Group by fermentation batch/condition; keep B2a/B2b together for grouped holdout. Also use chronological last 4 assay times as forecast evaluation. Never randomly split minute sensor rows, and never interpolate 64 offline assays into 86000 supposedly measured targets.
sources.label_guardrail: Rename scope to microbial biosurfactant fermentation monitoring/forecasting. No claim to reservoir oil-gain prediction or field microbial activity.

rejected_or_not_selected.reason: Four real lab hydraulic-fracturing MAT files are each 442 MB to 1.6 GB; over size cap.
Lab granite/marble fracture benchmark raw RAR is 2.4 GB; over cap.
CT scan raw ZIP is 15.3 GB. Small core photos are illustrations, not a labeled CV corpus.
Seismic imaging ZIP is 57.8 MB; over cap.
Downloaded 1.69 MB filtered AE moment-tensor archive; no self-contained unit/column documentation verified yet, so do not use for supervised metrics.
Small SAGD optimization code archive lead, not verified cyclic-steam measurements; do not reuse without checking.
